projects.title: NYC Open Data relaunch
projects.description: The city's Open Data portal relaunched on September 14, 2026, with improved dataset discovery, browsing by agency or category (climate, housing, food, walking and pedestrian), a submission process for the Open Data Project Gallery, and expanded getting-started resources including free monthly classes.
projects.why_interesting: The main entry point for every NYC dataset just changed how people find things, including the project gallery this scan draws on.

projects.title: Employer Violations Dashboard, 2026 edition
projects.description: Comptroller Mark Levine's annual, searchable database of private employers cited for health and safety violations, wage theft, prevailing wage violations, anti-union interference, and discrimination between 2024 and 2025, with the full dataset downloadable. Released around Labor Day, with the 2026 edition covered in NYC press starting September 4, 2026.
projects.why_interesting: Names specific employers, Amazon and Starbucks among them, by violation type rather than aggregating them into an anonymous count.

projects.title: NYC crash database frozen since June
projects.description: Streetsblog and Hoodline report that the Open Data feed underlying NYPD crash records has not updated since June 11, 2026, past the city's own August target for a fix, leaving map tools like Crashmapper and CrashCount silently missing months of crashes.
projects.why_interesting: A live example of a pipeline failure that makes downstream safety maps look falsely reassuring, worth flagging to anyone citing those crash maps right now.

projects.title: The Eleventh of September (Tape Art memorial archive)
projects.description: Rebuilt in 2026 by designer Gordon Wintrob, this site maps and lets visitors search all 490 tape-drawn figures Tape Art placed across four Manhattan zones in 2006, each representing one person killed at the World Trade Center on September 11, 2001.
projects.why_interesting: A 20-year-old civic art project turned into a searchable, mapped archive rather than a static photo gallery, published around this year's anniversary.

projects.title: UN System Data Commons
projects.description: Google and the United Nations launched an open-source, AI-ready knowledge graph unifying statistics from across UN agencies at data.un.org on September 17, 2026, built on Google's Data Commons platform and queryable via natural language or the Model Context Protocol. Twenty-six UN entities have committed data, with nearly 20 live at launch and a goal of 80 percent of UN statistical datasets by 2027.
projects.why_interesting: A single queryable layer over UN statistics that city and urban researchers currently have to pull from dozens of separate agency portals.

projects.title: Virginia affordable housing preservation dashboard
projects.description: HousingForward Virginia, the Virginia Housing Alliance, and Locus Impact launched a dashboard tracking Low-Income Housing Tax Credit units by expiration date, flagging more than 18,000 of the state's roughly 108,000 LIHTC units as losing affordability restrictions by 2030. Published September 17, 2026; the group says a bigger data update from the state housing authority is coming by year end.
projects.why_interesting: Turns an abstract tax-credit expiration schedule into a property-level early-warning list that local governments could act on before units convert to market rate.

projects.title: Heat Index Days by U.S. County
projects.description: New York Times Opinion piece using beeswarm plots and maps to show how many days a year each U.S. county spends above a 90-degree heat index and how sharply that has risen over three decades. Published September 5, 2026.
projects.why_interesting: County-level framing makes a national warming trend legible at the scale most people actually experience it.

projects.title: Visa-free reach of all 199 passports
projects.description: Interactive world map and bump chart by Akash Wadhwani tracking every passport's visa-free access and its ranking shifts from 2006 to 2026, plus scatter plots comparing visa-free reach against admission rates.
projects.why_interesting: Twenty years of ranking history in one interface, rather than the usual single-year passport-index snapshot.

projects.title: Hot spells and hospital deaths in Austria
projects.description: Complexity Science Hub, the Austrian Institute of Technology, and UBIMET built a heat-map and district-triangle visualization matching projected heat exposure against hospital mortality records across Austria, broken out by age group and decade.
projects.why_interesting: Pairs a climate projection with actual health-system outcomes rather than stopping at temperature forecasts, a model for tying weather data to hospital load.

projects.title: Hajj dates and temperatures in Makkah
projects.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Municipalities and Housing built a spiral visualization tracking Hajj dates across the Islamic lunar calendar's 33-year cycle against Makkah temperature ranges, alongside pilgrim demographic data.
projects.why_interesting: A government urban-data atlas taking on a calendar-and-climate problem specific to managing a city that hosts millions of pilgrims on a moving date.
